items.informal_name: Algebra Structure on Polynomial Ring over an Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {A : Type z} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : Semiring B]
  [inst_3 : Algebra R A] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (n : ℕ),
  ↑R (Polynomial.lcoeff B n) ∘ₗ (Polynomial.mapAlgHom f).toLinearMap = f.toLinearMap ∘ₗ ↑R (Polynomial.lcoeff A n)
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and an $ R $-algebra $ A $, the polynomial ring $ A[X] $ inherits an $ R $-algebra structure. This structure is defined by applying scalar multiplication coefficient-wise via the existing $ R $-algebra structure on $ A $, and the canonical algebra homomorphism from $ R $ to $ A[X] $ is given by composing the original algebra homomorphism $ R \to A $ with the constant polynomial embedding $ A \to A[X] $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Structure on Polynomial Ring over an Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {S : Type u_6} [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra S R]
  (f : PolynomialModule S S) (x : R),
  (Polynomial.aeval x) (PolynomialModule.equivPolynomial f) =
    (PolynomialModule.eval x) ((PolynomialModule.map R (Algebra.linearMap S R)) f)
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and an $ R $-algebra $ A $, the polynomial ring $ A[X] $ inherits an $ R $-algebra structure. This structure is defined by applying scalar multiplication coefficient-wise via the existing $ R $-algebra structure on $ A $, and the canonical algebra homomorphism from $ R $ to $ A[X] $ is given by composing the original algebra homomorphism $ R 	o A $ with the constant polynomial embedding $ A 	o A[X] $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence of Polynomial Rings Induced by Coefficient Mapping
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {A : Type z} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : Semiring B]
  [inst_3 : Algebra R A] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (f : A ≃ₐ[R] B), ⇑(Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv f) = Polynomial.map ↑f
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and $ R $-algebras $ A $ and $ B $, if there exists an $ R $-algebra equivalence $ f : A ≃ₐ[R] B $, then the induced $ R $-algebra homomorphism from the polynomial ring $ A[X] $ to $ B[X] $ defined by applying $ f $ coefficient-wise is itself an algebra equivalence. This means the map $ \text{Polynomial.map}(f) : A[X] → B[X] $ is invertible, with inverse given by $ \text{Polynomial.map}(f^{-1}) $, establishing an isomorphism between the polynomial rings that preserves both ring operations and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Preservation under Algebra Homomorphism on Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {A : Type z} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : Semiring B]
  [inst_3 : Algebra R A] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (p : Polynomial A) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.mapAlgHom f) p).coeff n = f (p.coeff n)
items.informal_description: For any $ R $-algebra homomorphism $ f : A \to B $, polynomial $ p \in A[X] $, and natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the image of $ p $ under the induced homomorphism is equal to $ f $ applied to the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $.

items.informal_name: Linear Equivalence via Polynomial Evaluation Compatibility
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {A : Type u_2} →
    {M : Type u_3} →
      [inst : CommSemiring R] →
        [inst_1 : Semiring A] →
          (a : A) →
            [inst_2 : Algebra R A] →
              [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] →
                [inst_4 : Module A M] →
                  [inst_5 : Module R M] →
                    [inst_6 : IsScalarTower R A M] →
                      {N : Type u_4} →
                        [inst_7 : AddCommMonoid N] →
                          [inst_8 : Module R N] →...
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $, an $ R $-module $ M $, an $ R[X] $-module $ N $ with scalar tower compatibility between $ R $, $ R[X] $, and $ N $, and an $ R $-linear equivalence $ f : M ≃ₗ[R] N $ satisfying $ f(a \cdot m) = X \cdot f(m) $ for all $ m ∈ M $, this constructs an $ R[X] $-linear equivalence between the polynomial evaluation module $ \text{AEval}(R, M, a) $ and $ N $. The equivalence is defined by composing $ f $ with the inverse of the canonical linear equivalence between $ M $ and $ \text{AEval}(R, M, a) $, ensuring compatibility with polynomial scalar multiplication by $ R[X] $.
